provenance.note: A case near the edge of CW validity assumptions: same circular-LEO, small-separation geometry as case (a), but requested over a HALF orbital period instead of a quarter. At n*t = pi exactly, Phi_rv's off-diagonal in-plane block becomes singular (src/cw.py Sec B.3); the boundary condition remains reachable (status singular-reachable), so src/model_selector.py returns a QUALIFIED CW decision, not a flat pass/fail. This exercises the model selector's documented targeting-conditioning signal (reference/SOURCE.md Sec B.3/D) without inventing a new universal numeric validity threshold: the separation ratio and duration itself are each comfortably inside validate_cw_use()'s existing heuristics (AC4) -- the borderline assumption here is specifically targeting conditioning at this exact transfer time, not locality or duration/regime.

request.natural_language: Earth is the central body. The target spacecraft is in a circular 350 km altitude orbit. Earth radius is 6378 km and gravitational parameter is 398600 km^3/s^2. The LVLH frame has x radial outward, y along-track in the target velocity direction, and z cross-track completing a right-handed frame. At t = 0, the chaser relative state is position [15 m, -200 m, 0 m] and velocity [-0.14 m/s, 0 m/s, 0 m/s]. Use two impulsive burns. After exactly one HALF of the orbital period, reach relative position [0 m, 0 m, 0 m] and relative velocity [0 m/s, 0 m/s, 0 m/s]. Return the two burn vectors and terminal relative state.

lvlh_convention.value: x radial outward, y along-track, z cross-track, right-handed

requested_outputs.value: burn vectors and terminal relative state

expected_model._comment: Per src/model_selector.py's targeting-conditioning signal: all six required assumption items remain 'supported' (circularity, locality, duration_regime, frame, other_physics, maneuver_assumptions are each individually unremarkable at this separation/duration); the half-period transfer time's singular-but-reachable Phi_rv is the sole boundary signal that qualifies the decision.
concerns: CW two-impulse targeting is singular but reachable at this transfer time; the returned velocity would be a non-unique SVD minimum-norm solution.
Qualified selection: verify this result against an independent numerical propagation (gmat-rendezvous-verification) before treating it as a clean pass.
expected_model.AC4_note: This fixture deliberately does NOT assert a universal numeric validity threshold (e.g. 'X% separation is the cutoff'); it only documents which already-implemented, already-documented signal (src/cw.py's two_burn_targeting SVD rank/residual check, surfaced by src/model_selector.py as targeting_conditioning) is borderline here.
